headline: Oyster Reefs Could Deliver $12 Trillion in Ecosystem Benefits
meta_description: Scientists identify 295,000 sq km of suitable habitat where restored oyster reefs could provide trillions in ecological and economic benefits.
summary_short: Restored oyster reefs could deliver an estimated $12 trillion in ecosystem benefits, according to new research identifying vast areas of suitable habitat.
body:
Oyster reefs around the world could deliver an estimated $12 trillion in ecosystem benefits if restored and protected, according to research from scientists studying marine conservation. The findings offer a striking reminder of what's possible when damaged natural systems are given a chance to recover.

Researchers identified 295,000 square kilometres of suitable habitat where oyster reef restoration could take root. This expansive area represents a genuine opportunity to revive ecosystems that have been depleted by centuries of overharvesting and coastal development. The sheer scale of potential restoration work underscores both the challenge and the prize: healthy oyster reefs filter water, provide nursery grounds for fish, and protect coastlines from storms.
quick_facts: $12 trillion in potential ecosystem benefits from restored reefs
295,000 square kilometres of suitable restoration habitat identified
Oyster reefs filter water and protect coastlines from storms
